title: Reduced induced closed subscheme structure on a closed subset: existence and uniqueness
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $T\subseteq X$ a closed subset. For an open $U\subseteq X$ let $\mathcal I_T(U)=\{f\in\mathcal O_X(U): f(t)=0\text{ in }\kappa(t)\text{ for all }t\in T\cap U\}$, $f(t)$ the image of $f$ in the residue field $\kappa(t)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Then: (1) $\mathcal I_T$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal O_X$; on an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] one has $\mathcal I_T(U)=I$, the unique radical ideal $I\subseteq R$ with $V(I)=T\cap U$, and $\mathcal I_T|_U=\widetilde I$. (2) The closed subscheme $i_T:T_{\mathrm{red}}\to X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] cut out by $\mathcal I_T$ (over each affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ it is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$) is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and $i_T(T_{\mathrm{red}})=T$. (3) Uniqueness: if $i':Z'\to X$ is a closed immersion with $Z'$ reduced and $i'(Z')=T$, then the ideal sheaf of $i'$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] equals $\mathcal I_T$, and there is a unique isomorphism $\varphi:Z'\to T_{\mathrm{red}}$ with $i_T\circ\varphi=i'$. The closed subscheme $T_{\mathrm{red}}$ is the *reduced induced closed subscheme structure* on $T$.

proof.text: $\mathcal I_T$ is a sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal O_X$. For $x\in U$ the map $f\mapsto f(x)$, $\mathcal O_X(U)\to\mathcal O_{X,x}\to\kappa(x)$ (germ followed by the residue map) [def-weil-residue-field] is a ring homomorphism and is compatible with restriction ($f|_V(x)=f(x)$ for $x\in V\subseteq U$, since germs are). Hence $\mathcal I_T(U)$ is an ideal of $\mathcal O_X(U)$ (if $f(t)=g(t)=0$ then $(f+g)(t)=0$ and $(af)(t)=a(t)f(t)=0$), and restriction maps $\mathcal I_T(U)$ into $\mathcal I_T(V)$, so $\mathcal I_T$ is a sub-presheaf of ideals. It is a sheaf: $\mathcal O_X$ is a sheaf, and if $U=\bigcup U_k$ and $f\in\mathcal O_X(U)$ has $f|_{U_k}\in\mathcal I_T(U_k)$ for all $k$, then every $t\in T\cap U$ lies in some $U_k$ and $f(t)=f|_{U_k}(t)=0$, so $f\in\mathcal I_T(U)$; the condition being pointwise, local sections of $\mathcal I_T$ that agree on overlaps glue in $\mathcal O_X$ to a section of $\mathcal I_T$.

source.place: Schemes, proof of Lemma 26.12.4 (Tag 01J3, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), first paragraph: 'Because of the local nature of the condition it is clear that I is a sheaf of ideals'

proof.text: Let $U\subseteq X$ be an affine open, $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$, $\iota_U:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$ the open immersion with image $U$ and $\mathfrak p_t$ the prime of $t\in U$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points]; $t\mapsto\mathfrak p_t$ is the homeomorphism $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$. The closed subset $T\cap U$ of $U$ corresponds to a closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec}R$, which by the definition of the Zariski topology [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is $V(J)=\{\mathfrak p: J\subseteq\mathfrak p\}$ for some ideal $J$. Put $I=\sqrt J$: it is radical, and $V(I)=V(J)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq] ($\sqrt{\sqrt J}=\sqrt J$). If $I'$ is another radical ideal with $V(I')=T\cap U$, then $V(I')=V(I)$ and $I'=I$ by the 'in particular' of [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq]. So there is a unique radical ideal $I\subseteq R$ with $V(I)=T\cap U$, i.e. $\{\mathfrak p_t: t\in T\cap U\}=V(I)$.

source.place: Schemes, proof of Lemma 26.12.4 (Tag 01J3, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), first paragraph: 'We may write T cap U = V(I) for a unique radical ideal I', with Algebra Lemma 10.17.2 (Tag 00E0, algebra-lemma-Zariski-topology)

proof.text: $\mathcal I_T(U)=I$ for $U,R,I$ as in the previous step. For $f\in R$ and $t\in T\cap U$ one has $f(t)=0$ iff $f\in\mathfrak p_t$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](a). Hence $f\in\mathcal I_T(U)$ iff $f\in\mathfrak p$ for every $\mathfrak p\in V(I)$ (these are exactly the $\mathfrak p_t$, $t\in T\cap U$), i.e. $\mathcal I_T(U)=\bigcap_{\mathfrak p\in V(I)}\mathfrak p=\sqrt I=I$ by [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq] and $I$ radical.

source.place: Schemes, proof of Lemma 26.12.4 (Tag 01J3, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), first paragraph: 'for any standard open D(g) of Spec(R) = U we have I(D(g)) = I_g by the same reasoning' (the reasoning written out)

proof.text: Clause (1): $\mathcal I_T|_U=\widetilde I$ and $\mathcal I_T$ is quasi-coherent. Identify $U$ with $\operatorname{Spec}R$ by $\iota_U$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points]; then $\mathcal O_X|_U=\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\cong\widetilde R$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-free-module] (rank $n=1$), with $\widetilde R(D(g))=R_g$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. The inclusion $I\to R$ induces $\widetilde I\to\widetilde R$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](1), which on each $D(g)$ is the inclusion $I_g\to R_g$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] (localization is exact), hence injective on a basis of opens and therefore injective (a section killed by the map has zero restrictions to a cover by standard opens, so is zero); thus $\widetilde I$ is the subsheaf of $\mathcal O_U$ whose sections over $D(g)$ are $I_g$. By step 4, $\mathcal I_T|_U$ is a subsheaf of $\mathcal O_U$ with the same sections $I_g$ over every $D(g)$. Two subsheaves of a sheaf with the same sections on a basis of opens are equal (a section lies in a subsheaf iff its restrictions to an open cover do, and every open is covered by standard opens). Hence $\mathcal I_T|_U=\widetilde I$ and $\mathcal I_T(U)=I$ (step 3). Since $\widetilde I$ is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] and every point of $X$ has an affine open neighbourhood [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal I_T$ is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent].

source.place: Schemes, proof of Lemma 26.12.4 (Tag 01J3, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), first paragraph: 'Thus I~ and I|_U agree (as ideals) on a basis of opens and hence are equal. Therefore I is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals'

proof.text: Clause (2), construction and image. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-closed-subscheme] applied to the quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals $\mathcal I_T$ there is a closed immersion $i_T:T_{\mathrm{red}}\to X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_T$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and for every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ the morphism $i_T^{-1}(U)\to U$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $I=\mathcal I_T(U)$ the radical ideal of steps 2-3. The image of $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is the set of primes of $R$ containing $I$ (primes of $R/I$ are $\mathfrak p/I$ with $\mathfrak p\supseteq I$), i.e. $V(I)=T\cap U$. So $i_T(T_{\mathrm{red}})\cap U=T\cap U$ for every affine open $U$; the affine opens cover $X$ [def-pc-scheme], so $i_T(T_{\mathrm{red}})=T$.

source.place: Schemes, proof of Lemma 26.12.4 (Tag 01J3, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), second paragraph: 'we may define Z as the closed subspace associated to I ... Z cap U = Spec(R/I) ... By construction the underlying closed subset of Z is T'

proof.text: Clause (2), reducedness. For an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $I=\mathcal I_T(U)$ is radical, so $R/I$ is a reduced ring ($\bar f^n=0$ means $f^n\in I$, so $f\in I$), and $i_T^{-1}(U)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ (step 6) is a reduced scheme by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-reduced-iff]. The opens $i_T^{-1}(U)$, $U$ affine, cover $T_{\mathrm{red}}$, and the local ring of $T_{\mathrm{red}}$ at a point $z$ is the local ring at $z$ of any open subscheme containing $z$; so every local ring of $T_{\mathrm{red}}$ is reduced and $T_{\mathrm{red}}$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme].

source.place: Schemes, proof of Lemma 26.12.4 (Tag 01J3, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), second paragraph: 'Z cap U = Spec(R/I) where I is a radical ideal and hence Z is reduced (by Lemma 01J2 lemma-affine-reduced)'

proof.text: Clause (3), the ideal sheaf. Let $i':Z'\to X$ be a closed immersion with $Z'$ reduced and $i'(Z')=T$, and $\mathcal I'$ its ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]: a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals such that, for every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $i'^{-1}(U)\to U$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I')\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $I'=\mathcal I'(U)$. The open subscheme $i'^{-1}(U)$ of the reduced scheme $Z'$ is reduced (its local rings are local rings of $Z'$) [def-pc-reduced-scheme], so $R/I'$ is reduced [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-reduced-iff], i.e. $I'$ is radical. The image of $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I')\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is $V(I')$ (as in step 6) and equals $i'(Z')\cap U=T\cap U=V(I)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq], $I'=I=\mathcal I_T(U)$ (step 3). Thus $\mathcal I'$ and $\mathcal I_T$ are subsheaves of $\mathcal O_X$ with the same sections on every affine open; affine opens form a basis of the topology of $X$ [def-pc-scheme] (an open subset of an affine open contains a standard open around each of its points, affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](b)), so $\mathcal I'=\mathcal I_T$ (as in step 5).

source.place: Schemes, proof of Lemma 26.12.4 (Tag 01J3, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), third paragraph: 'Z' cap U = Spec(R/I') ... By Lemma 01J2 the ring R/I' is reduced and hence I' is radical. Since V(I') = T cap U = V(I) we deduce I = I' by Algebra Lemma 00E0. Hence Z' and Z are defined by the same sheaf of ideals'

proof.text: Clause (3), the isomorphism. $i'$ and $i_T$ are closed immersions into $X$ with the same ideal sheaf (step 8 and step 6), so by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersions-equal-ideal-isomorphic] there is a unique morphism $\varphi:Z'\to T_{\mathrm{red}}$ with $i_T\circ\varphi=i'$, and it is an isomorphism. This is the uniqueness of the reduced closed subscheme structure on $T$; $T_{\mathrm{red}}$ is called the reduced induced closed subscheme structure (Schemes, Definition 26.12.5, Tag 01J4).
